note: Topical PDE4 inhibitors for mild to moderate atopic dermatitis; crisaborole (approved 2016) carries every cell, difamilast is approved, LEO 29102 failed Phase 2, DRM02 and AN2898 stopped.
label: Eczema · PDE4

engagement.population: Mild to moderate atopic dermatitis, ages 2 and older
engagement.confidence_note: Abstract-level reading; the FDA pharmacology review (PharmR) names the LPS/PHA/ConA-stimulated PBMC assays. First use proxied by the 2008 IND.
engagement.model: Stimulated human blood cells (PBMC cytokine release)
engagement.note: Crisaborole blocked PDE4 and cytokine release from stimulated human blood mononuclear cells in vitro.
engagement.short: Blocks cytokine release from blood cells
engagement.quote: A series of phenoxy benzoxaboroles were synthesized and screened for their inhibitory activity against PDE4 and cytokine release.
engagement.judgement: Model opens at the 2008 IND (proxy) with the 2009 paper as its first public record.

engagement.magnitude_basis: cytokine suppression (in vitro release vs lesional transcript expression)
engagement.population: Mild to moderate atopic dermatitis, ages 2 and older
engagement.confidence_note: Abstract-level reading. Pairing: the trial reads skin transcripts, the model reads cytokine protein from blood cells.
engagement.model: Stimulated human blood cells (PBMC cytokine release)
engagement.note: In patients' lesional skin, crisaborole lowered Th2 and Th17/Th22 cytokine pathways versus vehicle within 8-15 days.
engagement.quote: Crisaborole significantly modulated key AD biomarkers versus vehicle, including TH2 and TH17/TH22 pathways and epidermal hyperplasia/proliferation.
engagement.reason: Skin cytokine pathways fell in patients
engagement.judgement: Scored downstream: lesional cytokine mRNA is further down than PDE4/cAMP, and a different tissue from the PBMC assay. No cAMP or PDE4 activity was measured in patients.

dose.population: Mild to moderate atopic dermatitis, ages 2 and older
dose.confidence_note: Start year is a proxy: the second IND (Dec 2010) was reviewed in 2011; the 6-month rat study began June 2012. Exact minipig study dates not checked.
dose.note: Twice-daily crisaborole ointment up to 5% (3 months) and 7% (9 months) caused no systemic toxicity in minipigs.
dose.quote: In 3-month minipig dermal study (vehicle, 0.5%, 2%, and 5% crisaborole ointment B) with one-month recovery period, two daily applications did not produce any systemic toxicity at NOAEL of 5 percent.
dose.judgement: The class's dose model is taken as the toxic-end margin (decision 16): no efficacy-model exposure target was set; Phase 3 strength (2%) came from patient dose-ranging (AN2728-AD-204).

dose.magnitude_basis: minipig AUC0-24 at NOAEL (1,330-1,450 ng·h/mL) vs pediatric patient mean AUC0-24 (1,320 ng·h/mL)
dose.population: Mild to moderate atopic dermatitis, ages 2 and older
dose.confidence_note: Patient side from Paller 2016 (treatment-related AEs infrequent, mild to moderate) and the FDA review; registry date is the AD-301/302 results posting.
dose.note: FDA put the minipig NOAEL exposure about equal to pediatric patient AUC; patients at 2% twice daily showed no systemic toxicity. Retro: the minipig data were first public in the December 2016 FDA review, after crisaborole's own Phase 3 tolerability results (July 2015 topline, Paller 2016).
dose.quote: Taking into account, the pediatric mean AUC0-24 hr of 1,320 ng·hr/ml, the safety margin at the NOAEL of 5% crisaborole ointment is approximately equivalent to the maximum recommended human dose (MRHD) based on AUC comparisons.
dose.judgement: Scored same with margin_stated: the model stated a tolerated exposure at about the clinical one and patients were dosed to it without systemic toxicity; efficacy at that dose was positive. Rulings 2026-11-09: for dose the same drug's own earlier patient result counts; the minipig margin was first public in the 2016 review, after crisaborole's Phase 3 results were public, so same becomes retro.

efficacy.population: Mild to moderate atopic dermatitis, ages 2 and older
efficacy.confidence_note: Abstract-level reading: the abstract does not name the in vivo model; the 74% ear-edema figure is from the FDA PharmR.
efficacy.note: Topical crisaborole 5% cut phorbol-ester ear swelling in mice by 74%; this acute irritant model carried the class into patients.
efficacy.quote: 5-(4-Cyanophenoxy)-2,3-dihydro-1-hydroxy-2,1-benzoxaborole (AN2728) showed potent activity both in vitro and in vivo.
efficacy.judgement: Model identified from the FDA pharmacology review, which names only this in vivo efficacy model.

efficacy.magnitude_basis: mouse ear-edema inhibition (74%) vs ISGA success difference over vehicle (7-13 points)
efficacy.population: Mild to moderate atopic dermatitis, ages 2 and older
efficacy.confidence_note: Abstract-level reading of Paller 2016; registry results NCT02118766/NCT02118792 posted 2017-03-06.
efficacy.note: Both Phase 3 trials met the ISGA success primary endpoint, a modest effect over vehicle (32.8 vs 25.4%; 31.4 vs 18.0%); topline first public in Anacor's 13 July 2015 press release. Retro under the retrodiction ruling: the ear-edema model was first public in 2009, after a topical PDE4 inhibitor had already worked in atopic dermatitis patients (Hanifin 1996).
efficacy.short: Both Phase 3 trials met primary endpoint
efficacy.quote: More crisaborole- than vehicle-treated patients achieved ISGA score success (clear/almost clear with ≥2-grade improvement; AD-301: 32.8% vs 25.4%, P = .038; AD-302: 31.4% vs 18.0%, P < .001)
efficacy.reason: Reproduced known PDE4 efficacy in patients
efficacy.judgement: Kept same despite LEO 29102's failed Phase 2: that drug went in on a different model (mouse allergic contact dermatitis), so its miss does not land on this model. Rulings 2026-11-09: efficacy is a claim about the target, so a model first public after any PDE4 inhibitor's patient result is a retrodiction; Hanifin 1996 (doi:10.1111/1523-1747.ep12297888) had already shown a topical PDE4 inhibitor (CP80,633) reduce atopic dermatitis lesions in 20 patients, so the 2009 model reproduces a known result: retro. Year moved to the July 2015 topline press release (rule 6, earliest public date).

patient_trials.quote: Absolute Change in Eczema Area and Severity Index (EASI) Score From Baseline (Last Observation Carried Forward [LOCF])
Efficacy and Safety of AN2898 and AN2728 Topical Ointments to Treat Mild-to-Moderate Atopic Dermatitis
The OPA-15406 1% group was superior to the vehicle group in terms of the incidence of success based on the Investigator Global Assessment score at week 4 (P = 0.0328), which was the primary end-point
A Safety and Efficacy of DRM02 in Subjects With Atopic Dermatitis

efficacy.confidence_note: Paywalled; abstract only. The mouse allergic contact dermatitis model is named in the full text (checker-confirmed; web-search snippet) but not in the abstract. First use proxied by the Phase 2 start (Dec 2009).
efficacy.note: LEO 29102 went into patients on a mouse topical allergic contact dermatitis model, with dose-dependent skin TNF-alpha inhibition.
efficacy.quote: This effort culminated in identification of LEO 29102 (20), a potent, selective, and soft-drug PDE4 inhibitor with properties suitable for patient-friendly formulations giving efficient drug delivery to the skin.
efficacy.judgement: Separate system from crisaborole's phorbol-ester ear edema: a hapten allergic model used by LEO for its own candidate.

efficacy.magnitude_basis: EASI change vs vehicle: -2.86 best LEO 29102 dose vs -0.85 vehicle, p=0.08; no dose significant
efficacy.confidence_note: Registry results (NCT01037881) read directly; model side abstract-level. The sponsor paper called the Phase 2 efficacy 'clinically relevant' without reporting the primary endpoint.
efficacy.note: Phase 2 primary endpoint (EASI change at day 28) was not significant versus vehicle at any of five LEO 29102 strengths. The model was first public (2014) after other PDE4 inhibitors had worked in patients, so this is a failed retrodiction.
efficacy.short: Phase 2 primary missed at every dose
efficacy.quote: Absolute Change in Eczema Area and Severity Index (EASI) Score From Baseline (Last Observation Carried Forward [LOCF])
efficacy.judgement: Pairing: the registry's ANOVA p-values (0.27, 0.83, 0.08, 0.16, 0.14) set the status, not the sponsor's 2014 'clinically relevant efficacy' claim, which gave no primary-endpoint result (rule 7: the 2014 claim is not an admissible comparison). Active control pimecrolimus separated (p=0.04), so the trial could detect an effect. Rulings 2026-11-09: the model was first public in 2014, after Hanifin 1996 showed a topical PDE4 inhibitor (CP80,633) reduce atopic dermatitis lesions in 20 patients and after crisaborole Phase 2, so it is a retrodiction; it failed to reproduce LEO 29102's own result, so the status stays contra.

efficacy.confidence_note: Study date not given in the review; 2012 is a proxy (first Phase 2, NCT01702181, started Aug 2012).
efficacy.note: Difamilast's filed efficacy model was a mouse chronic contact dermatitis; it outperformed crisaborole there.
efficacy.quote: Difamilast showed efficacy in a mouse model of chronic contact dermatitis.
efficacy.judgement: Separate from LEO's acute allergic model: repeated hapten challenges, Otsuka protocol.

efficacy.magnitude_basis: mouse dermatitis score reduction vs IGA success over vehicle in Phase 2/3
efficacy.confidence_note: Abstract-level reading. Patient side: Hanifin 2016 (doi:10.1016/j.jaad.2016.04.001, primary IGA met at week 4, P=.0165), Saeki 2019 and the 2021 Phase 3 trials, all met their primaries.
efficacy.note: Otsuka set the mouse result beside difamilast's clinical efficacy: the model agreed with positive Phase 2 and 3 trials. Retro under the retrodiction ruling: the mouse data were first public after crisaborole's trials and Hanifin 1996 had shown topical PDE4 inhibitors work.
efficacy.quote: Difamilast, a novel selective phosphodiesterase 4 (PDE4) inhibitor, demonstrated significant efficacy without adverse reactions such as nausea and diarrhea in patients with atopic dermatitis (AD) and was recently approved in Japan.
efficacy.judgement: Dated 2023, when the model data were first public beside the trials. Rulings 2026-11-09: post-dating alone makes a retrodiction, judged on the date the model result was first public, not when it was run; the mouse chronic contact dermatitis data were first public (registry protocols from 2016, Hiyama 2023) after topical PDE4 inhibitors had worked in AD patients (Hanifin 1996; crisaborole Phase 3, July 2015), so same becomes retro.

efficacy.model: Human skin explants: dermal open-flow microperfusion with tissue cAMP
efficacy.note: LEO built a barrier-impaired human skin explant readout (free drug in dermal fluid, tissue cAMP) to explain clinical outcomes of its topical PDE4 inhibitors.
efficacy.quote: To investigate the difference in clinical efficacy in AD patients between two topical PDE4 inhibitors using dermal open flow microperfusion and cAMP as a pharmacodynamic read-out in fresh human skin explants.
efficacy.judgement: Opening entry at the model's first use, which came after both trials.

efficacy.magnitude_basis: explant target engagement (cAMP raised, dISF 2100 nM) vs LEO 29102 Phase 2 primary EASI endpoint not met
efficacy.confidence_note: Abstract-level. The paper treats LEO 29102 as clinically efficacious against LEO 39652 (not a class member); the registry primary endpoint for LEO 29102 was not significant.
efficacy.model: Human skin explants: dermal open-flow microperfusion with tissue cAMP
efficacy.note: Explants showed LEO 29102 engaged PDE4 in barrier-impaired skin, implying efficacy, but its Phase 2 primary endpoint failed.
efficacy.quote: Elevated cAMP levels were observed with LEO 29102 while no evidence of target engagement was obtained with LEO 39652.
efficacy.judgement: A retrodiction. The authors call it a match because they read LEO 29102 as clinically active. Against the registry primary (no dose significant, best p=0.08) it fails to reproduce the result, so contra. A near-miss trend could make this arguable; low confidence.

efficacy.note: Academic group tested difamilast in oxazolone-induced allergic skin inflammation, a common mouse model of atopic dermatitis.
efficacy.quote: In this study, we addressed this unsolved issue by analyzing the action of difamilast, a novel phosphodiesterase 4 inhibitor, on an oxazolone-induced skin allergic inflammation commonly used as a mouse model of atopic dermatitis.

efficacy.magnitude_basis: mouse ear inflammation reduction vs approved clinical efficacy
efficacy.note: Difamilast reduced oxazolone skin inflammation, reproducing the approved clinical effect.
efficacy.quote: Topical application of difamilast ameliorated skin inflammation in association with reduced IL-4 expression even when the treatment commenced 4 days after the initiation of oxazolone challenge, showing its therapeutic effect on atopic dermatitis.
efficacy.judgement: Takahashi (difamilast) and Calama 2024 (crisaborole) use one system, repeated oxazolone challenge on mouse ear; split into one track per drug. This entry is the difamilast track.

efficacy.note: Otsuka tested difamilast in MC903-induced AD mice for itch, ear thickness and barrier loss, after clinical approval.
efficacy.quote: Therefore, we evaluated the effects of difamilast on pruritus, dermatitis, and skin barrier dysfunction in MC903-induced AD model mice.

efficacy.magnitude_basis: scratching, ear thickness and TEWL reduction vs clinical IGA/itch response
efficacy.note: Difamilast cut scratching, ear swelling and water loss in MC903 mice, reproducing its known clinical effect.
efficacy.quote: One of the topical PDE4 inhibitors, difamilast, has been shown to be effective in the clinical treatment of AD.
efficacy.judgement: Stated comparison: the paper opens on clinical efficacy and reproduces it in mice; retro since run after the trials.

efficacy.note: Almirall ran crisaborole in a four-challenge oxazolone mouse dermatitis model, after crisaborole's approval.
efficacy.quote: The aim of this study was to comprehensively characterise a murine model of dermatitis and assess the similarity with the human disease, as well as to profile clinically relevant AD therapies.
efficacy.judgement: Opening entry of the crisaborole track on the oxazolone model, at its first use for crisaborole (2024).

efficacy.magnitude_basis: ear swelling, histology and cytokine signature vs clinical response to standard-of-care AD therapies
efficacy.note: Topical crisaborole inhibited oxazolone dermatitis in mice, reproducing its known clinical effect; run years after crisaborole's approval.
efficacy.quote: Oral (cyclosporine, prednisolone and baricitinib) and topical treatments (betamethasone, tacrolimus and crisaborole) were effective inhibiting the induced pathology, as well as modulating the cytokine gene signature of AD.
efficacy.judgement: Stated comparison: the authors profile therapies clinically effective in AD and call the model responsive to them; run after the 2016 approval, so retro.

safety.population: Mild to moderate atopic dermatitis, ages 2 and older
safety.confidence_note: Study date not in the review; 2010 is a proxy (IND-enabling local tolerance before the Dec 2010 IND).
safety.note: In rabbits the 2% clinical ointment was a mild to moderate skin irritant; mouse LLNA showed no sensitization.
safety.quote: In primary ocular and skin irritation assays in rabbits, 2% AN2728 ointment was tested as a mild to moderate irritant.

safety.magnitude_basis: local irritation grade in rabbits vs application-site pain incidence in patients
safety.population: Mild to moderate atopic dermatitis, ages 2 and older
safety.confidence_note: Pairing within the FDA package; the review does not link the rabbit result to the patient finding.
safety.note: Application-site pain (burning, stinging) was the one common adverse reaction: 4% on crisaborole vs 1% on vehicle. Retro: the rabbit data were first public in the December 2016 FDA review, after crisaborole's own Phase 3 safety results (Paller 2016).
safety.quote: The most common side effect of EUCRISA is application site pain, such as burning or stinging.
safety.judgement: Partial: rabbits graded erythema/edema, patients mainly reported burning or stinging. Label contact urticaria not scored against the negative LLNA, which tests delayed-type sensitization only. Rulings 2026-11-09: for safety the same drug's own earlier patient result counts; the rabbit irritation data were first public in the 2016 review, after Paller 2016 (epub July 2016) reported application-site pain, so same becomes retro.
